topic: How do lens prototypes' 15.4 dBi directivity and scan limitations influence LEO satellite orbital altitude and coverage zone planning?
consensus_response: The high directivity (15.4 dBi) of lens prototypes for LEO satellites increases RFI susceptibility due to the physical mechanism of interference between the beam's main lobe and side lobes. This is exacerbated by scanning limitations, which reduce flexibility in beam shaping. Orbital Diversity can be applied to mitigate this effect by adjusting the satellite's orbit to minimize exposure to terrestrial radio astronomy systems. However, this introduces trade-offs between signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and modulation schemes. Frequency Reuse can also be combined with Orbital Diversity to optimize LEO satellite constellation design and reduce interference.
